The paper I got the elevator operator stat from. Which doesn’t mean many jobs haven’t changed dramatically as a result of technology, of course. https://t.co/F7dGbApCyH

But it also means that no leader of a company, government, or any other institution has ever had to deal with a radically different socio-technical regime. The old approaches that worked through the ups-and-downs of the previous 75 years may not work for the years ahead.

The image comes from one of my first posts on OneUsefulThing right after the release of ChatGPT, based on the premonition that this time, things are going to be different.

If we avoid disaster, worth remembering humans are very good at muddling through.
https://t.co/Bm1p9YdweD

I think often about the fact that almost everyone working in the West has lived in a quite stable socio-technical period

Only 1 job out of 270 in the 1950 census is now obsolete (elevator operator)

2026 is similar to 1957 in a way that 1969 was not from 1900.

That may change. https://t.co/1ybpu5JlJV

I was watching the new Apple HomeView reviews and seeing that they hallucinate and fail to understand what's going on around them. Feels very bitter lessonable compared to whatever expert system they're trying to build. https://t.co/iLTax8XOdi

A good frontier model can reason about the state of the house; point out anomalies, safety issues, or things that are wrong; and solve problems for you. They have increasingly good spatial understanding from images. All of this is the things you want.

Google seems well-positioned in the home hub space, but the abilities of Google Home are far below what a model like Hydrogen is capable of. I don’t know what Apple & Amazon are going to do with their lagging models, using a Chinese open weights model seems unlikely.
